research.giants: 16 of 16 (8 AI, 8 paid media), last 10 posts each by web search on 10 November: about 150 posts. Ralph Burns and John Moran barely post on X, so their items are Perpetual Traffic episodes. Most posts show no like counts, so ranking is by spread, freshness and fit.
research.our_work: 112 Claude Code sessions (example figures; client work is left out of this public example).
research.creators: 11 of 11 core channels, 51 core winners, 18 in-window uploads. Scan 9 November 2026.

topics.title: Fable 5.2 Just Launched a Business. So I Gave It Mine.
topics.evidence: Mollick, 9 Nov: "I think it crosses the line into being a sort of Jagged AGI. Here, I have it launch a business..."
topics.ours: Run it on one real task at three effort levels
points: Mollick asked Fable for a business earning $20,000 a year on 20 minutes monthly.
It screened 22 ideas and chose Prebid Brief, tracking funded park and water projects.
He stopped at a demo: no real customers, so not truly running alone.
Test it on one real task at low, high and max effort first.

topics.title: Anthropic's Head of Claude Runs ONE Prompt Every Time a New Model Drops
topics.evidence: Albert, 9 Nov (about 472K views): "Read this entire project and find everything that's broken, inconsistent, inefficient, or no longer needed..."
topics.ours: His prompt, live, on three of our projects
points: Albert runs the same prompt on every project whenever a new model arrives.
It asks for everything broken, inconsistent, inefficient or no longer needed in the project.
Fix what you're sure about, then list the rest for your review.
Run it on your website, offers and automations each time models change.

topics.title: Stop Turning Off Your Best Ads (The Pros Are Begging You)
topics.evidence: Hott, 28 Jul: "I AM BEGGING YOU NOT TO TURN OFF HIGH SPENDING ADS"  · Moran, Perpetual Traffic 789, "Why Pausing Meta Ads Based on CPA Is a BIG Mistake!"
topics.ours: AI reads an account and says which ads are feeding the sales before you pause anything
points: Hott: turning off high-spend ads shifts budget, raising other ads' CPAs.
Hott says ad-level CPA and ROAS are irrelevant; judge the whole account.
Moran: Andromeda credits last click, so weak-looking ads may feed later sales.
Before pausing, have AI map which ads start journeys that end in sales.

topics.title: Google's New AI Just Went Public. Should Your Business Switch?
topics.evidence: Logan, 28 Oct: "Introducing Gemini 4 Carbon... SOTA on cyber, long horizon tasks, ranks #1 on Artificial Analysis V5"
topics.ours: Same business task in Gemini, Claude and ChatGPT, side by side
points: Logan says Carbon is a big jump over Argon, released two weeks earlier.
Claimed best on cyber and long tasks, and first on Artificial Analysis V5.
He reports cheating cut to zero and unsupported claims roughly halved versus Argon.
Run one real business task in Gemini, Claude and ChatGPT before switching.

topics.title: 16 Black Friday Leaks Costing You Money. AI Checks Them All.
topics.evidence: Shackelford, 22 Oct: "16 flows that quietly cost money during BFCM, and the check I run on each"
topics.ours: AI runs all 16 checks on a store in one go
points: Shackelford lists 16 BFCM flows that quietly cost money, with a check each.
He has Claude pull flow performance from Omnisend before running his checks.
His sheet catches discount stacking, dead tracking links and open VIP links.
Have AI run every flow check on your store before Black Friday.

topics.title: Karpathy Built His Own YouTube in 2 Hours. Here's the Business Version.
topics.evidence: Karpathy, 1 Nov: "I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos"
topics.ours: The same filtering on a lead list
points: Karpathy had Claude filter 43M Hacker News comments down to 6,454 videos.
A script stripped spam first; only the remainder went to Claude for labelling.
Claude tagged each mention as recommend, cite, joke or criticise; recommendations survived.
Apply the same staged filter to a lead list before any outreach.

topics.title: Google's AI Now Makes 15-Second Ads. I Made One for My Business.
topics.evidence: Logan, 5 Nov: Gemini Omni Flash 1.2, "longer video generation (15 seconds)... 30% lower price"
topics.ours: Make a real ad with it, then put it next to our AI presenter ads
points: Logan: Omni Flash 1.2 makes 15-second videos, up from 10 seconds.
Price dropped 30%, to about $0.07 per second at 720p.
Adds camera POV controls, multi-turn editing and less visual drift between shots.
Make a real 15-second ad, then test it beside your presenter ads.

topics.title: Stop Chasing ROAS. Plan Your Ads From Profit (AI Does the Maths)
topics.evidence: Tichenor, 17 Oct: "Plan spend from actual profit, not desired outcomes."
topics.ours: AI turns a P&L into an ad budget
points: Charley: plan ad spend from actual profit, not the outcomes you want.
Start with last month's profit; give a fixed share to next month's acquisition.
Early-stage brands might reinvest 80 to 90%; mature ones 50 to 60%.
Feed AI your P&L and let it set next month's ad budget.

topics.title: Claude Can Now Copy Any YouTuber's Editing Style
topics.evidence: Riley, 9 Nov: REA-Video, where "claude downloads a video from youtube and analyzes every frame... to extract the video editing style"
topics.ours: Copy a style, then apply it with our editing skill
points: Riley shared REA-Video, a circulating Claude skill: Reverse Engineer Anything, Video.
Claude downloads a YouTube video and analyses every frame to extract style.
Riley says with Fable it is very good; he tested it on stream.
Extract a style you like, then apply it with your own editing skill.

topics.title: Your "Book a Call" Button Is Losing You Sales
topics.evidence: Perpetual Traffic 811 (13 Oct, paraphrase): the booking calendar at the end of a funnel may be where sales are lost; and 814: "Are Wrong Leads Showing Up to Your Sales Calls?"
topics.ours: Our AI call centre answers the lead the moment they book
points: Episode 811 asks if your end-of-funnel booking calendar loses half your leads.
Show notes: the call booking calendar can kill your show rate.
In one client case, show rates rose about 20% when setters called every lead.
Call every lead the moment they book; AI can do it instantly.

topics.title: AI Hackers Are Here. 5 Things Every Business Owner Should Do This Week
topics.evidence: Brockman, 4 Nov: "we've found, validated, and prepared patches for almost 1,000 linux local privilege escalations... about $1,000 per vulnerability"
topics.ours: A plain checklist: passwords, 2FA, keys out of repos
points: Brockman: OpenAI found and prepared patches for almost 1,000 Linux privilege escalations.
OpenAI's write-up: 948 exploits for $1.2 million, about $1,280 each.
OpenAI warns an unpatched machine with any low-level account is effectively root.
This week: unique passwords, 2FA everywhere, keys out of repos, update everything.

topics.title: One Person Just Replaced a $60K/Month Growth Team With AI
topics.evidence: Holiday, 4 Mar: "I spent 12 years figuring out how to collapse a $60K/month growth team into one person"
topics.ours: Which jobs AI really does for us now; feeds "What Scaling With AI Actually Looks Like"
points: Holiday spent 12 years collapsing a $60K-a-month growth team into one person.
Claimed results: within 3.15% of forecast across $3B GMV, 32% revenue growth.
Method: break each role into tasks, systematise the mechanical work, encode it in software.
List your team's jobs, then show which ones AI now does for you.

topics.title: Stop Putting Up With Bad Software. Build Your Own in One Sentence.
topics.evidence: Karpathy, 3 Nov: "you can also just tell your Claude Code 'Create and deploy an extension for my browser...', works great"
topics.ours: Three one-sentence fixes for our own annoyances
points: Karpathy replied to a builder who made a Chrome extension called Honest Thumbnails.
His one sentence asked Claude Code to build a YouTube thumbnail extension with a toggle.
It swaps clickbait thumbnails for a real still from halfway through the video.
Write down three daily software annoyances and fix each with one sentence.

topics.title: Meta Might Be Spending Your Money on the Wrong Ads. Here's How to Check.
topics.evidence: Hott, 17 Apr: "META 'RELATED MEDIA' BUG: Here's an ad where 96% of spend went to ads OTHER THAN the one I thought it was"
topics.ours: AI checks where the spend really went
points: Hott found 96% of one ad's spend went to other media entirely.
Simply opening an ad's edit screen can make Meta add Related Media.
Check with a breakdown by Creative, then Related Media, at every level.
Export your breakdowns and let AI flag where the spend really went.

topics.title: Claude Duet Can Now Control Claude Code on Your Computer
topics.evidence: Riley, 8 Nov: "Claude Duet can now Control Claude Code that's running on your computer"
topics.ours: Run a real job from a phone
points: Riley says Duet now controls Claude Code running on your own computer.
He lists multiple computers, existing sessions, new sessions and real-time voice.
He pitches it as great for video editing and coding tasks.
Start a real job from your phone, then check and approve it later.

topics.title: How to Make People Actually Believe Your Ads
topics.evidence: Haynes, 30 Sep: "Back up your claims with third party data • Use timelines to anchor your points • Give multiple sources..."
topics.ours: AI checks an ad for every claim with no proof behind it
points: Haynes says back up every marketing claim with third party data.
He says use timelines to anchor your points and give dates.
He says give multiple sources of truth, not just your own word.
Run each ad past AI to flag every claim without proof behind it.

topics.title: 75% of People Have Never Really Used AI. Here's What the Top 0.2% Do.
topics.evidence: Karpathy, 11 Oct: about 6B people "have barely come in contact with LLMs at all"; about 20M see agents finish weeks of work from a prompt
topics.ours: Each level of the funnel, shown with our work
points: Karpathy's napkin maths: about 6 billion people have barely touched LLMs.
One to two billion use free chatbots, roughly like a better Google.
About 20 million see agents finish weeks of work from one prompt.
Pick one real job and hand it to an agent this week.

topics.title: The Next Big Agencies Will Be Half Software
topics.evidence: Holiday, 4 Nov 2025: "The next wave of 9 figure exits in eCommerce... SEANs — Software Enabled AgeNcies"
topics.ours: Our agency plus skills, as an example of it
points: Holiday predicts SEANs, not brands, SaaS or agencies, win nine figure exits.
A SEAN mixes SaaS scalability with agency human leverage and outcomes.
His agency builds 'software with an opinion' linking marketing and finance.
Package your agency's know-how as skills clients use between your calls.

topics.title: How the Man Who Built Claude Code Actually Works
topics.evidence: Cherny, 17 Sep: "I stopped managing sessions. I just send thoughts as they come, Claude splits them into threads"
topics.ours: His three habits (Projects, Code Review, Slides), copied by us
points: Cherny stopped managing sessions; he sends thoughts and Claude splits them into threads.
Code Review sends a team of agents to deep-review every pull request.
His Claude Slides habit: no more hunting for iPhone frame graphics by hand.
Pick one habit this week and let Claude remember how you work.

topics.title: Stop Checking AI's Work for Mistakes. Do This Instead.
topics.evidence: Mollick, 7 Nov: "the idea that the job of humans should be checking AI work for mistakes is likely not true today"
topics.ours: Where we still check, and where we don't any more
points: Mollick says worry about verifying AI output for factual errors is overdone.
He says recent models beat human experts, even PhDs, at checking facts.
Still check points of view, opinions and approaches, not just factual errors.
Stop proofreading AI for slips; spend your review time on judgement calls.

topics.title: Build an Ad Account That Runs Itself
topics.evidence: Tichenor, 17 Aug (paraphrase): build accounts that improve themselves, with automated rules pausing losers and scaling winners
topics.ours: AI writes the rules for one account
points: Tichenor treats automated rules as a core fundamental of his ad accounts.
His older rule: raise budget 20% when seven-day CPA meets target.
Rules pause spend automatically when performance misses the target threshold.
Ask AI to draft pause and scale rules for one account first.

topics.title: ChatGPT Can Now Build You a Custom Screen. Here's What to Make.
topics.evidence: Altman, 7 Oct: "ChatGPT can now generate a custom UI for you!"
topics.ours: Three screens a small business would use
points: Altman announced GPT-6 and Intelligent UI rolling out in ChatGPT for everyone.
Answers can now include charts, forms, buttons, checklists, maps and mini tools.
OpenAI's example: a recipe widget that rescales quantities for your guest count.
Try three screens a small business needs: quotes, bookings and weekly sales.

topics.title: Your Ads Working Too Well Could Kill Your Business
topics.evidence: Shackelford, 19 May: "Ads start working too well and the cash flow can't catch up"
topics.ours: AI cash-flow check before you scale spend
points: Shackelford has seen more CPG brands killed by scaling than by failing.
He grew BREZ to $90M+ in three years, spending over $50M on ads.
Plan cash 60 to 90 days out; size reserves for the worst week.
Before raising ad spend, have AI map when cash leaves and returns.

topics.title: AI Now Makes Consultant-Level Decks and Spreadsheets
topics.evidence: Albert, 24 Jul: "Opus 5 now produces near-superhuman level spreadsheets and slide decks that match what a consultant would make"
topics.ours: Our presentation skill, against a real brief
points: Albert says Opus 5 makes near-superhuman spreadsheets and consultant-level slide decks.
Albert framed it as progress made in just over six months.
Cherny says Claude Slides is now how he makes his own decks.
Test it on a real brief and judge against a consultant's deck.

topics.title: Why Every Brand Will Go Live (And Where AI Fits)
topics.evidence: Holiday, 15 Sep (5,424 views): "The end state to creative volume and authenticity is 'live'... I call it 'reality commerce'"
topics.ours: What AI can prep for a live show
points: Holiday says the end state of creative volume and authenticity is going live.
He calls it reality commerce: streaming, live shopping and daily live shows.
Winning brands cut each live session into five to ten clips within an hour.
Let AI draft your show outline, product notes and clip list before going live.

topics.title: I Ran My Whole Inbox From a 45-Minute Phone Call With AI
topics.evidence: Riley, 1 Oct: "just called my dot for 45 minutes and handled all my email / slack tasks for the day"
topics.ours: Try it for a day of our own admin
points: Riley spent 45 minutes on a call with his OpenAI dot, clearing email and Slack.
He did it with his phone in his pocket and AirPods in, walking.
His morning routine covers email replies, instructions for editors and planning the day.
Book one day of your own admin as a voice call and compare time saved.

topics.title: Hit the Google Ads Ceiling? It's Your Creative, Not Your Bids
topics.evidence: Perpetual Traffic 805 (25 Aug, paraphrase): stalled Google Ads is a creative strategy problem
topics.ours: AI writes new search-ad angles from customer calls
points: Burns says Google Search captures existing demand; it cannot create new demand.
His case: a B2B SaaS spending over $200K a month on Search, stalled.
Fix demand creation on Meta, YouTube and CTV; judge creative on hook and hold.
Use AI to mine customer calls for buyer-focused angles, not just user features.

topics.title: OpenAI Says Its New AI Is Built for Entrepreneurs. I Tested It.
topics.evidence: Altman, 3 Sep: "We hope it will begin to enable a new generation of entrepreneurship"
topics.ours: One business task in GPT-6 Astra against Claude
points: Altman hopes GPT-6 Astra will enable a new generation of entrepreneurship.
OpenAI calls it the best model for computer use, professional work and coding.
Brockman said he personally believes it is AGI, but readers should decide.
Run one real business task in Astra and Claude, then compare results.

topics.title: 10 Things to Fix Before Your Agency Can Scale
topics.evidence: Haynes, 28 Aug: "Sat down with two agency owners doing $247K/mo who want to scale to $1M. Here are the 10 things I told them"
topics.ours: Which of the 10 AI can do for you
points: Haynes advised two agencies at $247K a month aiming for $1M.
His first fix was collecting $12K cash upfront, not cutting cost per call.
He says stop solving every problem by adding headcount; stretch your current team.
Hand AI the tasks that would otherwise push you into a new hire.

topics.title: AI Agents vs Offshore Staff: Who Should a Small Business Hire?
topics.evidence: Maalouf, 12 Aug 2025: "the majority of normal skill level staff will be replaced with AI agents"
topics.ours: Our real costs for both
points: Maalouf says agencies chase AI agents as a shiny object to charge more.
He predicts most normal-skill staff will be replaced by agents doing daily tasks.
His company RemotelyX promotes trained overseas staff, claiming up to 83% savings.
Price the same role with both options using your real costs before hiring.

whittled: About 150 posts in. Dropped about half: jokes, replies, job moves, rows and personal posts.
Merged posts on the same thread. Strongest: Fable 5.2 (5 giants), "don't pause your best ads" (Hott, Moran, Burns), "one person replaces a team" (Holiday, Haynes).
Kept the top 30 by Part T score, at least 10 paid media, no giant more than 3.
Order: things that expire first (Fable 5.2, Gemini 4 Carbon, Black Friday on 27 Nov), evergreen later, AI and ads alternating.
Booked Wednesday and Friday recordings and the locked titles still stand: put them on their days and push these back, or post two that day.
notes: Ralph Burns's X is mostly from 2023 and John Moran's handle is unconfirmed: their rows link to Perpetual Traffic episodes.
Rows marked paraphrase come from search summaries. Open the post or episode before quoting it on camera.
T12, T18 and T30 are older evergreen posts (March 2026, Nov 2025, Aug 2025): ideas, not news.
